insider_note: The absence of air is the whole definition. With air the same alkane would burn to carbon dioxide and water; without it, heat alone breaks the chain into lower alkanes, alkenes and hydrogen.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: Pyrolysis is the decomposition of an
alkane into smaller molecules by strong
heating in the absence of air.
It is used most on the higher alkanes.
The products are lower alkanes, alkenes
Applied to alkanes the process is also
steps.why: The definition carries two conditions at once: heat is the only reagent, and air is excluded. Excluding the air is what makes the alkane break up instead of burning, which is why the products are smaller hydrocarbons and hydrogen rather than carbon dioxide and water.
common_mistakes: Calling it combustion. Pyrolysis is carried out in the absence of air, so nothing burns.
Giving carbon and hydrogen as the products. The products are lower alkanes, alkenes and hydrogen.
Leaving out the words in the absence of air. That condition is part of the definition.
steps.memory_tip: Heat alone and no air: the chain breaks into smaller pieces.
steps.margin_note: Name the strong heating, the absence of air and the kind of products.

lines: Hexane heated to 773 K breaks in more
So a mixture of products is obtained,
steps.why: One example makes the definition concrete, and hexane shows the point that matters: the chain can break at more than one place, so pyrolysis gives a mixture. Each equation still balances on its own.
common_mistakes: Calling the single equation the complete answer. Pyrolysis gives a mixture, so say so even when only one equation is written out.
Writing an equation that does not balance. Every fragment equation must account for all six carbons and all fourteen hydrogens.
steps.memory_tip: The same hexane can break at different places, so several equations are correct.
steps.margin_note: Give one worked example and say that a mixture of products is formed.
